fix(facts): a run declared while stamps fail answers why; one lane per declared run; recording v4 (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.6pj.d8n)

Review (second high) findings on #641:
- A declared run the document lacks reads pending only while stamps
  succeed; while they fail it answers the stamp's failure, so a request
  does not wait out its deadline on a run that cannot land.
- The follow keeps one document lane per declared run on its entry.
- RECORDING_VERSION is 4: request lines require a cwd and documents carry
  runs.
- The README says a recording holds what each shell and file source read.

fix(facts): a replay opens the view at each request's directory; a run declared into a disposed follow is refused (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.6pj.d8n)

Review (medium) findings on #641:
- Every recorded request carries an absolute cwd (SessionRequest), and the
  demo's play opens the view at each request's directory, as the daemon
  moves a session's view to the entry its request names, so a session that
  moves directories replays its runs under the digests it recorded.
- The follow's owner readings and run readings are separate computeds.
- A run declared into a disposed follow throws by name instead of starting
  a run nothing ends.
- The law marker on the depth binding is restored.

fix(facts): a replay opens its view where the session's opened; a run's lane keeps its reading while its value holds; each declared run holds its own entry (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.6pj.d8n)

Review (high) findings on #641:
- The recording proves the session's directory from its opening request,
  and the demo's replay opens its view there, so a shell source's digest
  matches wherever the demo runs.
- A run's lane hands out one reading while its entry holds one value
  (computed, structural), so a restamp for another fact republishes
  nothing and a JSON source's torn-write settle is not restarted.
- Each run declaration holds its run in a Holds of its own, closed by its
  release or the follow's dispose: no whole-set re-declaration per change,
  and no dispose order that throws.
- The recording arm finds a coming run by each digest's last document.
- Dead DEPTH_FUNCTIONS export and stale directory-scope comments removed.

feat(facts): a session's shell and file sources run into its facts document, and a recording replays them with nothing read or spawned (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.6pj.d8n)

A config's `shell` and `file` sources ran beside the facts seam: the
variable registry held their runs directly, so a recording carried none of
them and a replay started each one on the replaying machine, drawing it
before its first result.

The document gains `runs`, each declared run's reading and watch fault by
identity digest. Each facts arm offers the run lanes a view's registry
declares through: the in-process arm holds the runs and stamps them into the
follow's document, which the lanes read; the recording arm's lanes read the
reached document, pending only while a later document holds the run and
failed, naming it, once none does. Every shell and file source is a session
view's, since only a view has a document to read; one run per identity is
the digest's to decide. The render event carries `runs=` and `runsPending=`.

feat(links): the one MouseDown1Status binding is constant text; each session carries its renderer's click (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.b2l.5v7)

Every renderer on a tmux server now binds the same text, so no renderer owns
the binding and two renderers no longer fight over it. What differs per
renderer (its url-handle command under its home, its name, its binding mac)
rides on the session it draws, as @cc-candybar-click beside
@cc-candybar-renderer. The binding runs that option on a ccb range, shows a
tmux message where a session carries no click, and runs the user's own
binding otherwise.

The user's binding lives only in the binding's else-branch, read back from
list-keys as a command list, so the @cc-candybar-binding-prior record goes
(the bind unsets one an older build left). Ours is recognised by shape, and
every one of ours chained over the user's is peeled off. The restore is one
tmux call that tmux guards on whether any session still names a renderer,
and it runs once per bound period.

The status-line click verb is now `range`.

feat(links): a tmux range id is ccb plus a base36 link id from a counter in the home's state; the URL digest goes (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.b2l.e1n) (#640)

* feat(links): a tmux range id is ccb plus a base36 link id from a counter in the home's state, held per session and surface and minted once a frame; the URL digest goes (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.b2l.e1n)

- A feed encodes each lane once a frame through one encoder per (session,
  lane), so the tmux row and `frames --lane tmuxStatus` share one minting.
- The tmux lane's encoder holds an LRU table keyed by the link's URL (cap 256):
  a redraw reuses its id, so an animating row mints nothing.
- The home's counter reserves ids a block at a time (hi/lo), so a restarted
  renderer starts past every id the last one issued.
- A counter fault is every bar's warning; its retry is the allocator's own
  timer, one attempt a still period, so it clears with nothing minting.
- Stats gain linkIds { minted, reused, evicted, reservations, faults }.

* fix(links): a still row drawn while the counter was faulted gets its ranges back; the count is written through the one atomic write, flushed before its rename (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.b2l.e1n)

A frame is unchanged only when every lane encodes it as it did the last,
since the tmux status line's encoding reads ids the answers do not carry.
writeAtomic fsyncs before renaming, so a crash leaves the old file or the
new one, never an empty one. The reused stat names what it counts, and the
inventory docs stop naming the digest and the per-subscriber encode.

* fix(links): a status row's table evicts once a frame is drawn, never a link the frame holds (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.b2l.e1n)

A row of more links than the cap kept evicting its own earlier links, so
every frame minted them again. The cap's comment says what it is for: a
click resolves against the frame the row last drew, not the table. The
inventory docs stop naming the digest and the old tmuxStatusFrame call.

* fix(links): a status-row click carries the mac its binding was signed with, since a range id is a counter anyone can guess (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.b2l.e1n)

Any web page can open a cc-candybar:// URL, and a status-row click resolves
to a signed link the row draws, so with counter ids a page could run any
action on the row. The binding now carries the link key's mac over its
server's socket, and linkAt refuses a click without it before resolving
the range; a range resolves only to the frame's own entries. Spec section
18 carries the mac in the binding. A closed allocator issues no id and
writes nothing, and a block that would pass the last count is a fault, not
a file its own reader refuses.

## [1.201.1](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar/compare/v1.201.0...v1.201.1) (2026-11-06)

### Bug Fixes

* **facts:** a recording replays a session's picks and open menus: each draw carries the state it read (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.6pj.gs4) ([#639](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar/issues/639)) ([f62952f](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar/commit/f62952f2c7273142b5ad4581bd6d5f05bd29044f))
fix(disk): the fake walks a new entry's parent, makes a `..` folder, refuses a move into itself and forgets a failed watch; path derivation takes a Filesystem (candybar-testing-ihvy.y10)
fix(disk): the fake moves, removes, writes through links and resolves `..` as the kernel does; repo-configs is made on the tree that watches it; the real disk is owned (candybar-testing-ihvy.y10)

feat(disk): files and their watch events go through one filesystem port, first used by the watcher registry and the binary watch (candybar-testing-ihvy.y10)

A Filesystem port (src/disk/) with one adapter over fs, an in-memory fake whose writes emit the events a watch would on the clock, and one contract both pass. The watcher registry, its delivery owner, plugin storage, folder identity, the link walk and the binary watch read the disk through it; IdentityRead and BundleStat are gone. A lint rule bans fs outside the adapter, with an allowlist of the files still to move.
refactor(apply): a synchronous click needs no in-flight bracket on the idle clock; journaled refuses an async handler (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.1dh.c3l)
fix(apply): a probe link is refused by no client's leaving; the doctor stamps the hints it reads; the click error keeps its record's shape (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.1dh.c3l)
fix(apply): each click failure is its own held message; a fault's stack reaches the log; no gather starts after close (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.1dh.c3l)

feat(apply): no turn awaits a launch; a doctor step is an effect, and a held click error accumulates (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.1dh.c3l)

A turn is a synchronous call: its body cannot be async (Synchronous<T>), a
render request never waits behind another session's probes, and no draw can
read a click half landed. A doctor step describes an effect; the performer
gathers after the click's turn through a recording view, and the landing
checks the gather's read set and config in the turn that writes the report.
Lands yth: a click error held while the last is live joins it.
